newsitem.title: USA: Democratic donor boasts of Clinton ties in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Democratic donor boasts of Clinton ties in Turkey.

text.p: Roger Tamraz, a major contributor to the Democratic Party, boasted to Turkey's prime minister that he possessed direct access to President Bill Clinton, the Los Angeles Times reported on Sunday.

Tamraz's effort "to exploit his purported ties to Clinton -- described in detail by Turkish officials -- provides a glimpse of the value of White House access for promoters of overseas business deals," the newspaper said.

"In short, that access could pry open doors in foreign capitals. In Tamraz's case, Turkish officials said, they were sufficiently impressed so that they checked with the White House to see if he really did have access to Clinton," the Times continued.
Tamraz was described as a Lebanese-American businessman who wanted to build an oil pipeline from the Caspian Sea to Turkey.

His meeting with Turkish Prime Minister Tansu Ciller in September of 1995 "came a week before he attended the first of six White House meetings with President Clinton. All six were group events for large Democratic donors. Tamraz did not meet, one-on-one, with either Clinton or Vice President Al Gore," the newspaper said in an article from Washington.
Tamraz told the Times he did not speak of Clinton to Ciller.
Turkish officials who attended the meeting told the Times that Tamraz told Ciller he was to see Clinton the following week, leaving the impression that it would be a private meeting.
Access to the president was mentioned "when negotiations with the Turkish government on his pipeline deal were going badly for him," Turkish government officials told the newspaper.

The Turkish government doubted Tamraz and conducted a background check, finding that "among other things, Tamraz was wanted in Lebanon on charges stemming from the collapse of his bank -- charges that Tamraz says were politically motivated by his powerful enemies in Beirut," the Times reported.

"The Turks ultimately rejected Tamraz's plan and no new pipeline has been built from the Caspian Sea oil fields to serve as an alternative to the only pipeline in place today that runs through Russia," the Times said.
